newsitem.title: INDONESIA: MOTOCROSS-TOP RIDERS SET TO START 125CC SEASON IN INDONESIA.
newsitem.headline: MOTOCROSS-TOP RIDERS SET TO START 125CC SEASON IN INDONESIA.

text.p: The world's 15 top motocross riders clash on Sunday in the ancient Indonesian city of Yogyakarta when the 1997 world 125cc championships get under way.
Among the 51 riders in the race, which launches this year's season, are Britain's Paul Malin and Italy's Alessandro Puzar.

Qualifying practice was set to start on Saturday afternoon with Marlin, riding a Yamaha, and Puzar, on a TM, expected to face stiff competition from 1994 world 250cc champion Bob Moore of the United States.
Absent this year, however, was the 1996 125cc world champion Sebastian Tortelli of France, who has decided to race in 250cc this year, race organisers said.
Puzar told reporters he was determined to start the season with a win. "I will do my best to win this first round and also the next ones. If Malin says he wants to win, so do I," he said.
Moore shared Puzar's optimism and said he was adapting to Yogyakarta's blazing sun. "The most important thing is that the vehicle is okay and the physical conditions are alright," he said.
Puzar returned to 125cc bikes after racing in the 250cc class in 1996.
Organising committee spokesman A.R. Loebis said there were eight Indonesian riders in this year's race, the only event in the series held outside Europe in the last two years.
From Yogyakarta, the 125cc riders move to Pernes, France, for the second race on April 13. The last of the season's 12 events will be in the Netherlands on August 31.
